name: Ringo Corponation Slipframe Courier Bike — 'The Needle'
product_name: Ringo Corponation Slipframe Courier Bike — 'The Needle'
description:
The Slipframe Courier Bike is Ringo Corponation's flagship personal mobility platform, engineered specifically for Meridian 88's layered urban geography — the stacked overpasses, the collapsed transit corridors, the narrow maintenance alleys between arcology foundations. Its chassis is built from a carbon-titanium hybrid lattice that flexes under stress rather than fracturing, allowing the bike to absorb impacts from debris, guardrails, and glancing collisions that would total a conventional frame. The electric drivetrain is whisper-quiet at low speeds and produces a distinctive high-frequency whine at full acceleration that riders call 'singing the needle.'

The Needle's defining feature is its Drift Assist Neural Interface — a handlebar-mounted haptic feedback system that reads the rider's grip pressure, body lean, and micro-corrections and feeds predictive routing suggestions directly through the handlebars as vibration patterns. Experienced riders describe it as the bike 'thinking ahead of them,' subtly steering toward gaps in traffic or flagging surface hazards before they're visually apparent. The system integrates with Ringo's broader Drift Mesh network, pulling real-time traffic and threat data when in range. Off-network, it falls back to onboard LIDAR and a local hazard model.

Couriers swear by the Needle. So do runners, fixers, and anyone whose life depends on being somewhere else very quickly. The bike's slim profile allows passage through gaps too narrow for any four-wheeled vehicle, and its low heat signature makes it difficult to track on standard thermal surveillance. In Meridian 88's courier culture, the Needle is aspirational — a mark of a serious professional. The worn chrome variants ridden by veteran couriers, scratched and re-welded a dozen times, are considered more prestigious than new models.

cultural_context: Courier culture in Meridian 88 treats the Needle as a rite of passage. First-year couriers save aggressively to afford one, and the bike's condition becomes a biographical record — each weld scar and replaced component tells the story of a close call survived. Ringo Corponation leans into this, running a well-known certification program called the Slipframe Rating that grades riders on speed, route efficiency, and delivery integrity. A high Slipframe Rating is a legitimate professional credential in courier circles and carries weight in the broader runner community as evidence of skill under pressure.
story_hooks: A Needle recovered from a crashed courier contains a Drift Mesh log that shouldn't exist — the bike was in a location that was supposedly under total communications blackout.
Ringo Corponation's Slipframe Rating program has been quietly weaponized — top-rated couriers are being recruited for something that isn't delivery work.
A courier's Needle has developed a Drift Assist behavioral pattern nobody can explain — it keeps routing toward the same condemned building regardless of destination input.
The players need to move something across the city in under forty minutes with surveillance grids active. The only option is a Needle and a rider who knows the city better than they know themselves.
